text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures end slightly higher, resting at support near 97.30, traders see ranges with focus clearly on U.S. Short-end of yield curve could get support from mark. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 97.39, up 0.07 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts retreated from the day's high, locking in only a small gain despite successful auction, dealers sentiment is bullish with good support at lower levels and gilts could continue to outperform short-term, volume high as auction hedges are unwound. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-07/32, up 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French debt finished a second rough day in a row lower with PIBOR interest rate futures succumbing again to franc weakness as non-residents sold amid fears of labour unrest. The September notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 122.96, down 0.16 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to easier levels, just off the day's lows, in late trade along with other European bond markets and as investors awaited to see any details from Italy's 1997 financial budget, gains in U.S. Treasuries and JGBs helped stem losses while the steady lira helped give some support. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 115.40, down 0.05 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. treasury securities were marginally negative and confined to extremely tight trading ranges at midday, without any fresh economic data to provide direction, traders focused on the highlight of Wednesday's sparse calendar -- the Treasury's auction of $12.5 billion in five-year notes. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-29/32, down 01/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.98 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) futures ended dramatically higher on unexpectedly gloomy results of BOJ's "tankan" survey. BOJ official's bearish comments on capital spending after release of survey triggered another rally towards close. Key 10-year JGB yield above six-month low of 2.995 percent.In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 121.81, up 1.20 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity surged on Wednesday, with arbitrage-driven retail deals dominating. In marks, JFS launched its expected 350 million markthree-year deal at 10 b.p. over Bobls. BNG set a 500million mark five-year bond and Bank Austria issued a 250 million mark December 2000 deal. The EIB set a 250 million stg December 2000 bond, which will be priced to yield three b.p. over gilts. Scott Fetzer, part of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, issued a $100 million five-year bond.
